reasons: The clause plainly binds Customer (Meridian) with a worldwide, undefined-scope non-compete on developing, marketing, selling or acquiring 'any product or service that competes with Vendor' for 24 months post-term — squarely a deviation and past the walk-away threshold (post-term >12 months, undefined scope).
The redline deletes § 12.4 in full, which is exactly the playbook preferred remedy for a non-compete binding us; deterministic checks confirm no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains.

Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, prefixed correctly, states what changed and why, and offers the narrowed fallback (single named product, term only, ≤12 months, internal-development and acquisition carve-outs) consistent with the rule's fallback position.
Severity 'high' as configured is appropriate; no smaller edit would reach the preferred position since the entire sentence is the restriction.
